source.head: be1b665fc272dc73e38acf9415f0518956fbda6d
source.selected: Construct one local generator per channel, apply them in a batch, and sum after application. Single-qubit supports use six-dimensional slices for N >= 6; smaller systems and general ordered supports use the direct tensor contraction. No diagonal coefficients are merged across channels.
source.complexity: For K channels of bounded support, local dissipative work is O(K D^2). With O(N) channels and an O(ND) Hamiltonian matvec, the full RHS is O(N D^2). The density matrix is O(D^2); batching can materialize a channel axis, so compiled temporary memory and worker RSS are reported separately.
source.current_measurements: forward_and_precision, accuracy, gradient, upstream7, rhs_counts, dense_control and comparisons were rerun against the frozen final source. Each generic/new comparison records the final source SHA256. generic disables only the N >= 6 slice specialization and preserves per-channel arithmetic.
source.historical_data: historical_forward and original_large preserve earlier measurements and are explicitly historical. Only upstream N=3..6 enters the final figure/table. The final N=7 values for all four methods come from one fixed-CPU four-way mirrored cohort, so the table and upstream speedup use exactly the same measurements. Earlier final-source N=7 paired/three-way runs are retained separately. There are no upstream dense measurements at N=8..10.
source.kernel_profile: diagnostics.kernels uses a prototype numerically identical to the final implementation before formatting: old is the correct generic contraction, new is the selected batched slice application. These isolated kernels ran on a separate pinned CPU with no other task from this experiment on that core. The final end-to-end comparisons provide the claimed speedups.
source.phase_profile: diagnostics.phases and diagnostics.candidates are the initial, pre-optimization N=9,10 diagnosis. Callback phase barriers include materialization, dispatch and callback overhead and are not used as end-to-end performance measurements.
source.other_candidates: Direct einsum did not materially improve RHS time. Axis-1 vmap still compiled to two transpose/copy operations. Reusing (H rho)^dagger for the right action was not adopted: it requires Hermitian rho, while the API also evolves non-Hermitian operators, and an opt-in flag would expand the interface. Leading real/imaginary stacking gave inconsistent small changes and was not adopted. Premerged generators and diagonal coefficients fail the strong-X/weak-Y-or-Z test. A conditional diagonal-only variant preserved correctness but was slower. Historical candidate records are retained in rejected_candidates, not presented as final performance.
source.size_cutoff: Preliminary mirrored trials at N=6,7,9 compare the correct generic contraction with the selected slice kernel. These have two steady observations per method and are distinguished from the final four-observation N=9,10 comparisons.
source.large_accuracy: N=9,10 tight-tolerance TC trajectories are single accuracy-only solves. QuTiP and converged references use the unchanged physical model. Timing claims use separate warmed repeated runs.
source.reference: QuTiP DOP853 rtol=1e-14, atol=1e-15, max_step=0.04, normalize_output=False. Independent QuTiP Vern9 trajectories check convergence at N=8,9,10. Error metrics span all 51 saved states.
source.hardware: Shared Intel Xeon Platinum 8458P CPU. One pinned logical CPU and one BLAS/OpenMP thread per comparison; no GPU. Different experiments run on distinct cores. Affinities and loads are retained in individual records.
source.timing: The main curves use two mirrored three-way cycles, or four-way cycles for the final N=7 cohort, giving four warmed observations per method. Paired controls use two ABBA cycles. Compilation, first execution and steady time are separate. Runtime comparisons at a fixed tolerance also report actual error; the supplemental Dopri8/Adams comparison uses nearby measured errors.
source.tight_accuracy_supplement: The final plotted Dopri8 1e-15/1e-16 points and Adams 1e-14 control were collected on the same fixed CPU as the main N=8 curve, after that scan completed. Two mirrored three-way cycles give four observations per configuration. Earlier tight runs on other cores are retained separately and do not determine the plotted supplement or matched-accuracy conclusion.
source.validation_execution: The first full-check attempt was stopped during pytest collection after xdist auto selected 88 workers despite an eight-CPU affinity. It was restarted with PYTEST_XDIST_AUTO_NUM_WORKERS=8. Benchmark workers retained their one-CPU affinity throughout. The shared-host timings and all raw repetitions are retained without discarding observations.
source.gradient: Eight-qubit TC reverse-mode derivatives of final Z0 with respect to drive amplitude and damping rate use tolerance 1e-12 and are compared with independent high-accuracy QuTiP-Liouvillian tangent equations. Compilation plus first gradient execution is reported separately from steady forward times. No new steady gradient timing is claimed.

quality.pylint: Library/tests, root examples and both example subtrees: 10.00/10

model.hamiltonian: 0.7 sum_i Z_i Z_(i+1) + 0.3 sum_i Z_i + (0.6 cos(0.9 t) + 0.2) sum_i X_i
model.collapse: sqrt(0.08) sigma^-_i and sqrt(0.03) Z_i on every qubit
model.representations: TC uses PauliStringSum2MVP and local jumps; QuTiP uses sparse operators; upstream TC uses dense operators.

methodology: Shared Xeon Platinum 8458P; one logical CPU and one BLAS thread per comparison; normalization disabled; four warmed measurements in symmetric order. Raw rows retain affinity and wall/process timings. All workers import both libraries and construct the common physical inputs. Worker RSS includes that setup, solver construction/compilation and the full returned trajectories.
